definition: Exact resistance allele or explicitly unresolved/truncated resistance-gene framework.
detection: AMRFinder or curated nucleotide/protein reference with allele-specific constraints.
containment: May occur inside a cassette, captured segment, transposon, resistance region or plasmid backbone.

definition: Named protein-coding gene without an antimicrobial-resistance assignment.
detection: Curated feature reference or gene caller plus functional annotation.
containment: May occur in cassettes, mobile elements, accessory regions or plasmid backbone.

definition: Mobility gene such as tnpA, tnpR, tniA, tniB, tniQ, tniR or tns genes.
detection: Curated component reference or protein-family model; exact role retained.
containment: Part of an IS, unit transposon, Tn402-type module or related mobile element.

definition: Integron integrase gene intI, with class/allele retained when known.
detection: IntegronFinder or curated intI reference.
orientation: Coding direction; the class-1 5-prime conserved segment runs towards attI and opposite intI.
containment: Part of a minimal integron and normally within its 5-prime conserved region.

definition: Usually one promoterless ORF, occasionally two, plus its cognate attC recombination site.
detection: Cassette reference or oriented ORF-to-attC reconstruction; ORF alone is a cassette fragment.
containment: Member of a cassette array; may be interrupted or reduced to a remnant.

definition: Recognisable but incomplete cassette, ORF or attC remnant that cannot be promoted to a complete cassette.
detection: Partial reference match or incomplete ORF-attC evidence.
orientation: Inferred only when ORF or attC evidence supports it.
containment: May remain in a cassette array or interrupted integron.

definition: Cassette recombination site; seven bases begin the cassette and the remainder lies downstream of its gene.
detection: IntegronFinder attC model or exact cassette reference.
containment: Child of a complete cassette, cassette remnant or cassette array.

definition: One or more tandem gene cassettes downstream of attI and Pc.
detection: Ordered, consistently oriented cassettes and attC sites connected to an integron platform.
containment: Child region of an integron; contains cassettes and remnants.

definition: Primary integron recombination site adjacent to intI and the cassette array.
detection: Integron class-specific motif/reference and positional support from intI/Pc.
orientation: Defines the start of the cassette array.
containment: Part of the minimal integron platform.

definition: Integron cassette promoter, including named variants and P2 when activated by the 5-prime-CS GGG insertion.
detection: Variant-specific nucleotide motif in the 5-prime conserved segment.
orientation: Transcribes the cassette array away from attI.
containment: Part of the minimal integron platform/5-prime conserved segment.

definition: Class-1 integron 5-prime conserved segment, with variants such as 5CS_GGG distinguished.
detection: Exact/partial curated sequence match.
orientation: Runs towards attI and opposite intI.
containment: Part of a class-1 integron.

definition: Class-1 integron 3-prime conserved segment including qacEdelta1 and sul1 where present; not terminated automatically at qacEdelta1.
detection: Exact/partial curated sequence match plus downstream structural evidence.
orientation: Runs away from the cassette array.
containment: Part of a class-1 integron and may connect to downstream modules.

definition: Named element end such as IRL, IRR, IRi, IRt, IRalt or a subterminal IS1111-family IR.
detection: Exact/near-exact end motif with element-specific length and positional support.
orientation: Name and flat flag side preserve which outer boundary is represented.
containment: Boundary child of the element it delimits; fragments remain explicit.

definition: Target-site duplication/direct repeat with exact sequence, length and evidence state.
detection: Equal flanking sequence at candidate boundaries using element-specific length and tolerated offsets.
containment: Associated with the transposition event, never used alone to assign element identity.

definition: Recombination/resolution site, retaining resI, resII and resIII subsites when resolved.
detection: Curated nucleotide reference and expected position relative to tnpR/tnpA.
containment: Part of a Tn3-family or Tn402-type transposition module.

definition: Exact named IS comprising its transposase region and characteristic ends; family-level labels are insufficient for structural inference.
detection: Exact/variant reference match plus end evidence; incomplete copies retain fragment state.
orientation: Transposase direction; block arrow points to IRR.
containment: May interrupt another element or delimit a composite/pseudo-compound structure.

definition: Named mobile group-II intron, separate from insertion sequences.
detection: Exact intron or reverse-transcriptase reference.
containment: May interrupt genes or mobile elements.

definition: Insertion-sequence-common-region element using rolling-circle transposition and lacking conventional paired IR/DR boundaries.
detection: Exact rcr/ISCR reference plus oriIS and terIS evidence.
containment: May be associated with an adjacent captured segment.

definition: ISCR rolling-circle origin site.
detection: ISCR-family-specific motif and position relative to rcr.
orientation: Defines the origin side of an ISCR capture unit.
containment: Child of ISCR or an ISCR capture structure.

definition: ISCR rolling-circle termination site, which may be inefficient and permit adjacent DNA capture.
detection: Family-specific termination motif with structural context.
containment: Child of ISCR or an ISCR capture structure.

definition: Adjacent sequence mobilised with ISEcp1, ISCR or another one-ended capture mechanism.
detection: Boundaries derived from IRR/IRalt or oriIS/terIS plus cargo and DR evidence.
orientation: Follows the capture element's active end.
containment: Child of a TPU/capture unit; must not be absorbed into an unrelated adjacent transposon.

definition: A feature inserted into and breaking the collinearity of a host feature.
detection: Split host-reference alignment plus an intervening feature or unclassified sequence.
orientation: Records host and inserted-feature orientations independently.
containment: Links the interrupted host pieces and inserted feature without deleting either.

definition: Unannotated sequence longer than 50 bp between known features.
detection: Coordinate subtraction after all accepted features are placed.
containment: Gap within the current locus; not a biological element call.

definition: Recognisable fragment whose exact parent feature remains unresolved, including possible divergent or assembly-error sequence.
detection: Significant partial match lacking diagnostic sequence or coherent boundaries.
orientation: Retained only when supported by the match.
containment: May be nested in a region but cannot define a confident compound element.

definition: Plasmid replication-initiator/replicon feature used to identify an outer plasmid backbone.
detection: PlasmidFinder or curated replicon reference.
containment: Plasmid backbone, not a core mobile-resistance component.

definition: Plasmid vegetative replication origin.
detection: Replicon-specific motif/reference and positional context.
containment: Plasmid backbone.

definition: Plasmid origin of transfer.
detection: MOB-family-specific motif/reference and relaxase/conjugation context.
containment: Plasmid transfer/backbone region.

definition: Plasmid replication, maintenance, regulation, partition, conjugation or transfer gene.
detection: Functional protein model and plasmid-context evidence.
containment: Plasmid backbone or transfer region.

definition: Named plasmid non-coding RNA feature.
detection: Curated ncRNA model/reference.
containment: Plasmid backbone or accessory region.

definition: Outer-layer plasmid gene assigned to conjugation, stress, metabolism, non-conjugative mobility, virulence/defence, toxin-antitoxin, metal/biocide resistance, antibiotic resistance or other function.
detection: PlasAnn-style functional annotation with retained category and evidence.
containment: Plasmid backbone or accessory region; category does not itself imply mobility.
